 Microsoft raises Indian cloud prices by 15.7%, cuts them in China by up to 8.5%
 Monday, 16 November 2026, 03:36 
 Photo source: The Register 
 The roundup also covers a Sega outage and email-address leak, India’s export ban on battery-recycling residue, Alibaba’s plan to list its chip unit and a Japanese proposal to explore a satellite constellation. 
 Microsoft price changes
 Microsoft’s new prices for commercial cloud services take effect on January 1, 2027. Customers in India will pay 15.7 percent more for cloud services and up to 20 percent more for some on-premises offerings. Prices in New Zealand will rise by 10 percent. In China, where Microsoft delivers its cloud through local partner 21Vianet, costs will fall by up to 8.5 percent. Australian prices will drop by 4.5 percent, while prices in Norway will fall by 5.9 percent.
 This is reported by The Register .
 Microsoft sells its services in local currencies at rates equivalent to its US prices, and adjusts prices around the world as exchange rates shift.
 Advertisement 
 Sega outage and email leak
 Sega’s ALL.Net and Aime services, which connect arcade games across locations, suffered an outage. The services include administrative tools for arcade operators and features for gamers such as pre-payment to play, high-score and profile recording, and networked gaming. After discovering unauthorized access to servers, Sega suspended some services on November 1. At least 13 games and services were unavailable until around November 15.
 Sega has not explained what went wrong. It told customers the incident was not a data breach and that payment information was safe. Separately, email addresses of some Sega newsletter subscribers leaked through Arara Co., a third party Sega uses to send some emails. No other personal data leaked from Arara. Sega warned newsletter recipients to watch for suspicious messages.
 Alibaba plans to list T-Head
 Alibaba announced its intention to float its chip-design business T-Head on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The filing describes T-Head as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China,” suggesting Alibaba does not expect buyers elsewhere in the world to be keen to acquire its chips.
 The filing says the listing “allows a more efficient deployment of Alibaba Group’s financial resources.” It should also mean T-Head can more easily find third-party customers.
 India bans exports of battery-recycling residue
 India’s government banned exports of “Lithium-Ion battery Black Mass,” a powdery substance produced during battery recycling. The government said the material contains recoverable quantities of lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese.
 “It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese,” 
 - The government’s announcement
 The government said the ban “will increase domestic recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals, thereby reducing import dependence and the associated foreign exchange outgo. It will also strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing, electric vehicles, energy storage and clean-energy technologies.” It added: “Further, the measure will advance the circular economy and ‘urban mining’, reducing reliance on primary mining, while supporting environmentally sound recycling of this hazardous material within the country in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.”
 Japanese companies to explore satellite constellation
 NTT, Mitsubishi Electric, MUFG Bank, the Development Bank of Japan and NTT DOCOMO signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly explore developing and operating a large satellite constellation.
 “will examine the technical and business feasibility of commercializing a diverse range of services enabled by mega-constellations, including communications, Earth observation, satellite-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), and space data centers.” 
 - The five companies
 Mitsubishi Electric already works with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) to develop and manufacture rockets. MUFG Bank and the Development Bank of Japan regularly back large infrastructure projects, while NTT and NTT DOCOMO have advanced communications expertise. The companies did not set a deadline for delivering a plan.
 Advertisement 
 If the companies decide there is a business opportunity, they will likely need to look beyond Japan for launch capacity: JAXA does not currently have a reusable launch vehicle and has a modest launch cadence compared with private launch operators.
